doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Unreleased recordings and what she did before the stroke
summary: Her group's recordings were not released; she mostly conducted before the stroke and has done little since coming to Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: We did, but they didn’t release it or something like that. I didn’t play you the first song that was on the tape. That was with my small group.
That she just played from the radio date?
But I thought that was My Reverie from Dizzy’s . . .
No. When she – the very first thing . . .
Oh, that was just the introduction to it. I see.
. . . before she talked at all. Because Hale Smith – all of those things was talking about that tune that I did.
Because I’d never heard that before.
I haven’t done anything out here. I came out here when I had the stroke and everything.
But you were playing up until that time, right?
